national_raw_news.content: Prime Minister Narendra Modi will hold bilateral talks with the President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, in Tashkent today. The two leaders will review cooperation in trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people domains at the Presidential Palace. Akashvani correspondent reports that today Prime Minister Narendra Modi will first attend a yoga program organised by the Yoga Federation of Uzbekistan and after that he will directly go to the palace of Uzbekistan President Shavkat Mirziyoyev , where both the leaders will participate in bilateral talks. The leaders will review cooperation in the areas of trade and investment, defence, digital connectivity, energy, education and people-to-people relations at the Presidential Palace. Cooperation between the two countries is continuously increasing in the field of defence, but both countries will focus on mining, especially rare earth minerals and metals like gold and other useful minerals. Besides this, the field of medicine, agriculture and skill development, as well as finding new avenues of connectivity, can be a focus of discussion between the two leaders. Due to the Prime Minister’s efforts, trade between the two countries has increased by 300 percent in the last 10 years. Together, the two countries are aiming to double the current 1 billion dollar trade in the coming years. In this regard, some important agreements may be signed today. Earlier, the Prime Minister reached Tashkent, the capital of Uzbekistan, for his two-day visit to the Central Asian country yesterday evening. The Prime Minister was received by the President of Uzbekistan, Shavkat Mirziyoyev, at the airport. The Prime Minister laid a wreath at Yangi Uzbekistan Park in Tashkent, honouring Uzbekistan’s rich history, heritage and national spirit. Later, he was given a warm welcome by the Indian and Uzbek community in a traditional manner. There were performances of Kathak dance by Indian artists, Indian songs by Uzbeki artists and musical instruments by the artists of both countries.

national_raw_news.content: Nepal’s flash flood death toll has risen to 675 as search and rescue operations continue amid renewed rainfall and fears of further flooding. Nearly 2,400 people remain missing, including at least 320 foreign nationals. More than 4,400 people have been rescued or evacuated, including 261 foreign tourists who had lost contact. Akashvani correspondent reports that the Nepal Police reported that 675 bodies have been recovered from eight districts, with the highest numbers reported in Chitawan, Nawalparasi East, and Nawalparasi West. Over 15,000 security personnel have been deployed, while helicopters are carrying out repeated sorties to rescue stranded people and deliver relief supplies. According to officials in the hard-hit Rasuwa district, search and rescue operations resumed yesterday after being temporarily halted because of rain and fog. The Nepal government has issued a fresh alert for flooding in the Bhote Koshi River and urged residents living along the river to remain cautious. The National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority has reported an increased flood flow in the river. The Rasuwa District Administration said it has heard an increase in water flow and advised people in areas near the Bhote Koshi River in the Rasuwa, Nuwakot and Dhading districts to exercise caution. It said further updates will be provided as more information becomes available. The Bhote Koshi is a fast-flowing Himalayan river originating in Tibet. Seven people have also died on the Chinese side of the border, with more than 550 reported missing. The Mugling-Kathmandu highway, a major road link connecting the capital with other parts of the country, reopened yesterday after remaining closed since Wednesday. But several other roads remain blocked or difficult to access.

national_raw_news.title: 16 mins ago | National 24 108 Indian nationals rescued so far in Nepal following flash floods: Ministry of External Affairs
national_raw_news.content: The External Affairs Ministry has said that 108 Indian nationals have been rescued so far in Nepal following a flash flood tragedy on Wednesday. In a social media post, External Affairs Ministry spokesperson Randhir Jaiswal said that contact was re-established with around 50 Indian nationals who were earlier uncontactable. The Ministry said that 275 Indian nationals are reportedly missing and around 128 people of Indian origin, holding other nationalities, also remain missing. As per a local government source, 598 Indian nationals crossed into Nepal from China in the last two days. Meanwhile, 900 Indian Nationals who are yet to depart from China are safe and the Indian Embassy in Beijing is in touch with them directly or through the local government. The Ministry added that the Government of India has been working in close coordination with the Nepali and Chinese authorities for the early rescue and relief efforts of those affected by the floods. A round-the-clock Control Room has been established in the Ministry of External Affairs and the Indian Embassies in Kathmandu and Beijing have 24/7 helplines operational. It said both Embassies have also remained engaged with all the relevant stakeholders to ensure effective coordination of search, rescue and relief efforts. Government of India has offered the National Disaster Response Force to support Nepal’s search and rescue efforts and also mobilised immediate humanitarian assistance with Indian Air Force aircraft carrying emergency relief material to Nepal. In the meantime, External Affairs Minister Dr S Jaishankar said that a fourth aircraft sortie, a C130J Hercules with 11 tonnes of assistance, was sent to Kathmandu yesterday. In a social media post, Dr Jaishankar said that the aircraft is carrying a 13-member Indian Army tunnel rescue team with specialist equipment based on the recce team’s on-ground assessment to assist the ongoing search and rescue efforts of Nepali disaster response teams. In addition, a 19-member contingent of six forensic teams is also being sent to assist in the analysis of DNA samples for identification of mortal remains. A total of 68.5 tonnes of relief material comprising essential medicines, portable generator sets, food packets, water purification tablets and technical equipment have been airlifted to Kathmandu so far. The Minister said that additionally, 16 trucks carrying equipment for a 230 feet Single Lane Modular Steel Bridge have reached Nepal. Besides, equipment for the installation of seven more Bailey bridges will be supplied soon and Technical teams for their installation are expected to reach shortly.

national_raw_news.title: National Sports Day being observed today; Prime Minister Modi pays tribute to Major Dhyan Chand 29 Aug 2026 | 2:11 PM 169
national_raw_news.content: National Sports Day is being celebrated across the country today to commemorate the birth anniversary of one of India’s greatest sporting icons, Major Dhyan Chand. Prime Minister Narendra Modi today paid homage to the Indian Hockey Legend Major Dhyan Chand on the occasion of National Sports Day. In a social media post, Mr Modi said that Major Dhyan Chand’s brilliance in Indian hockey continues to inspire generations. Extending his greetings to all sports lovers, the Prime Minister said that their dedication, passion and determination make the nation proud. The day celebrates India’s rich sporting heritage and encourages people to make sports a regular part of their daily lives. National Sports Day 2026 is being observed as a three-day nationwide campaign under the pillars of Tribute, Play and Move. This year, National Sports Day is being celebrated under the call, Ek Ghanta Khel Ke Maidan Mein”. Various sporting activities are being organised across the country to mark the occasion. In Delhi, Union Ministers Dr Mansukh Mandaviya and Arjun Ram Meghwal participated in a cricket match under the campaign. Talking to the media, Dr Mandaviya called upon people to spend at least one hour on the playing field every week to remain fit and healthy. He said a fit youth and a healthy society are essential for building a prosperous nation. Mr Meghwal said he plays badminton every day. He said sports help people remain healthy and fit and also help in keeping stress away. The government has been making sustained investments in India’s sporting ecosystem, with the results increasingly visible on the global stage. India’s performances at major international sporting events reflect the country’s growing strength across Olympic, Paralympic and multi-sport disciplines. In the Union Budget 2026-27, over 4400 crore rupees were allocated to the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports, compared to just around 1200 crore rupees in 2013-14. India’s Olympic journey has witnessed a significant transformation in recent years. The country won two medals at Rio 2016, seven at Tokyo 2020 and six medals at Paris 2024. India’s performance at the Paralympic Games has also improved remarkably. The medal tally rose from four at Rio 2016 to 19 at Tokyo 2020. At Paris 2024, India recorded its best-ever Paralympic performance with 29 medals. India has also consistently improved its performance at the Asian Games. The country won 57 medals at the 2014 Asian Games and improved its tally to 69 in 2018 and scripted history by winning a record 107 medals in 2023. Initiatives such as Khelo India, the Target Olympic Podium Scheme, and Khelo India Rising Talent Identification are strengthening the sporting ecosystem and helping athletes prepare for competition at the highest level.

national_raw_news.title: BJP to organise community-focused gatherings for Mann Ki Baat programme across Gujarat 3 hours ago 47
national_raw_news.content: Bharatiya Janata Party (BJP) has planned a series of community-focused gatherings across Gujarat for the 137th episode of Prime Minister Narendra Modi’s Mann Ki Baat today, with senior party leaders set to listen to the programme alongside youth, farmers, professionals and community members. According to party leaders, National General Secretary Dr Satish Poonia will join members of the Rajasthani community at Sardar Smarak Bhavan in the Shahibaug area of Ahmedabad. Chief Minister Bhupendra Patel will listen to the programme at Booth No. 172 in the Ghatlodia Assembly constituency in the Thaltej area of the city. State BJP president Jagdish Vishwakarma will attend a youth-focused gathering at Pramukh Arcade in the Kudasan area of Gandhinagar. Union Jal Shakti Minister C. R. Patil will listen to the programme with chartered accountants and company secretaries at the Surat City BJP office in Udhna. At the same time, BJP National Vice-President Varsha Doshi will join young farmers at Dudhai in Muli taluka of Surendranagar district. The party has also arranged thematic programmes. State minister Sanjaysinh Mahida will attend ‘Mann Ki Baat – Nari Shakti Ke Saath’ at the BAPS Shri Swaminarayan Temple at Yogi Farm in Piplag Chowkdi of Nadiad district. State general secretary Aniruddha Dave will attend ‘Mann Ki Baat – Kisan Aur Pashupalakon Ke Saath’ at Shishumandir in Bidada of Mandvi taluka. In the Chandkheda area of Ahmedabad, State Vice-President Gautam Gediya and Mayor Hitesh Barot will attend ‘Mann Ki Baat – Anusuchit Samaj Ke Saath’ at Sant Shri Sadaram Bapa Community Hall. Party leaders said similar programmes would be held at all its booths across Gujarat, where party leaders, elected representatives, workers and citizens would listen to the broadcast.

To use standard view, enable JavaScript by changing your browser options. होम All Factsheet Factsheet Details Social Welfare India's Higher Education Sector प्रविष्टि तिथि: 30 AUG 2026 10:08 AM A Decade of Growth, Access, and Inclusion Building India’s Knowledge Ecosystem: A Decade of Progress Higher education is a cornerstone of India’s journey towards a knowledge-based economy and a key pillar of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 . The policy envisions an education system that promotes holistic, multidisciplinary learning and advances the goals of SDG 4. Sustainable Development Goal (SDG) 4 focuses on ensuring inclusive and equitable quality education and promoting lifelong learning opportunities for all. The Ministry of Education conducts an annual survey of Higher Education Institutions in India. The All India Survey on Higher Education (AISHE), conducted annually by the Ministry of Education, provides a comprehensive evidence base on Higher Education Institutions (HEIs) across the country. The data helps track the progress of higher education reforms under NEP 2020, identify emerging gaps, and inform policy responses. A Growing Higher Education Footprint According to AISHE reports, India’s higher education network has expanded significantly over the decade. The number of universities increased from 760 in 2014–15 to 1,289 in 2023–24, representing a growth of 69.6 % . The number of colleges rose from 38,498 to 48,246 , an increase of 25.3% . Standalone institutions increased from 12,276 to 15,221 , registering about 24% growth. This expansion reflects a widening institutional base and greater capacity to serve learners across the country. It has strengthened the reach of higher education, supported broader participation, and contributed to building a more accessible, diverse, and inclusive knowledge ecosystem for India’s future . Increasing Student Enrolment: Advancing Equity and Inclusion Higher education enrolment in India has risen steadily over the past decade, growing 31.5% from 3.42 crore students in 2014–15 to 4.50 crore in 2023–24. The Gross Enrolment Ratio (GER) in higher education rose from 23.7% in 2014–15 to 29.5% in 2022–23, and further to 30% in 2023–24. This steady increase reflects growing access to and participation in higher education, supporting NEP 2020's target of raising the GER to 50% by 2035. From 2014-15 to 2023-24 , level-wise percentage increase in total enrolments was: Ph.D 1.17 lakh to 3.43 lakh (192.89%); Post Graduate 38.53 lakh to 57.85 lakh (50.15%); Under Graduate 2.71 crore to 3.45 crore (27.27%); Diploma 25.08 lakh to 33.15 lakh (32.22%); Certificate 1.70 lakh to 2.08 lakh (22.55%); Integrated 1.41 lakh to 5.69 lakh (301.36%). ​​​​​​​ Female enrolment in higher education has witnessed steady growth over the past decade. It grew by 42.2% , rising from 1.57 crore in 2014–15 to 2.24 crore in 2023–24 , outpacing the growth in total enrolment during the decade. national_raw_news.title: FSSAI Issues Prohibition of Sale Order for Compounded Hing from Two Major Spice Brands ... - PIB
national_raw_news.content: Ministry of Health and Family Welfare FSSAI Issues Prohibition of Sale Order for Compounded Hing from Two Major Spice Brands Over Substandard Quality Posted On: 29 AUG 2026 2:34PM by PIB Mumbai Mumbai, August 29, 2026: To protect consumer interests and ensure food safety, the Food Safety and Standards Authority of India (FSSAI) has issued a Prohibition of Sale order for Compounded Hing (Asafoetida) manufactured by two prominent spice brands: M/s Everest Food Products Private Limited and M/s Laljee Godhoo and Company (LG Brand Unit). Following a consumer complaint regarding the quality of Compounded Hing of a specific brand, the FSSAI initiated comprehensive market surveillance covering all major brands in the market. Primary laboratory test reports from this surveillance indicated that Compounded Hing products from both Everest and LG were substandard. The FSSAI conducted legal sampling directly from the centrally licensed units of M/s Everest Food Products Private Limited and the LG Brand Unit, both located in Mumbai. These samples were sent to a primary laboratory for further testing. Additionally, the FSSAI collaborated with the Gujarat State FDA to conduct a joint inspection and sampling at the state-licensed unit of Everest Food Products Private Limited in Umbergaon, Gujarat. The primary laboratory confirmed that all legal samples of Compounded Hing collected during these operations were substandard. Under the FSS (Food Products Standards and Additives) Regulations, 2011, Compounded Hing is an admissible category constituted by blending Raw Hing, Gum Arabic, starches, and flours. The regulations dictate a minimum addition of Raw Hing to guarantee at least a 5% alcohol soluble extract in the final Compounded Hing product. The laboratory findings revealed significant deviations from these safety standards: Low Alcohol Soluble Extract: The tested Compounded Hing samples contained only 0-3% alcohol soluble extract, falling significantly short of the mandated 5% minimum. This indicates that the manufacturers were adding 30-40% less of the required Raw Hing into the consumer products. Excessive Starch Content in Raw Hing: The FSSAI also sampled six varieties of Raw Hing alongside finished goods at the LG Brand Unit in Mumbai. While FSSAI standards cap starch content in Raw Hing at a maximum of 1%, the laboratory confirmed that all six LG Raw Hing varieties contained between 15% and 32% starch, classifying them as sub-standard. By regulation, Raw Hing itself must contain a minimum of 12% alcohol soluble extract. Given that multiple batches of Compounded Hing were observed to be non-compliant with established quality standards, the FSSAI has formally issued a Prohibition of Sale order to M/s Everest Food Products Private Limited, Mumbai, and the LG Brand Unit, Mumbai. This administrative action is a preventive measure executed to safeguard public health and protect consumers' interests. Furthermore, the FSSAI has directed the involved Food Business Operators to submit a comprehensive action plan detailing how they will rectify these malpractices and ensure the production of standard Compounded Hing for consumers. The manufacturers have also been advised to initiate a voluntary recall of all substandard products currently in the market. *** Supriya Ghaytadak/Yash...
